items: Adaptive Structural Evolution Boundary (ASEB): mechanics of evolvability.
Framework studies conditions for continued evolution and aims at formal boundary models, simulations, permeability metrics, phase-transition tests and evolvability benchmarks.
Ongoing theoretical development and experimental-framework construction.
What determines whether a system can continue changing the mechanisms by which it adapts?

Evolution/evolvability are proposed to require accessible feedback, structural change, new representations and new transformation pathways; meaningful distinctions and structural-threshold crossings are proposed prerequisites for deeper adaptive regimes.
adaptation -> structural transformation -> continued evolvability; distinction -> representation -> optimization -> evolution.
Definitions for improvement Delta A, evolution Delta Gamma, evolvability Delta E, causal/epistemic/ontological permeability and adaptive boundaries.
Source relates ASEB conditions for evolvability to Ancestor Intelligence selection/direction toward future transformers; endpoint remains unresolved.
Operational scales for adaptation depth/permeability/boundaries/phase transitions, endpoint identity, and execution standing remain unresolved.

Core principles propose preserved future-change mechanisms, accessible feedback, representation-mediated adaptation, representation expansion, capability/evolvability divergence, correction preservation and structural-boundary evolutionary transitions.

optimization -> adaptation -> structural evolution -> continued evolvability; environment -> feedback -> representation update -> structural change; reality -> representation -> action -> feedback; distinction -> representation -> transformation -> selection -> evolution.
Representation roles, adaptation-depth definitions, adaptive-boundary roles and evolutionary closure.
State/generator/evolvability depth distinctions and protective-versus-restrictive boundaries.
Examples span learning, algorithms, scientific/education processes, language, mathematics, computation and chemistry/life/culture/technology transitions.
When do boundaries preserve identity while permitting evolution, and what structural conditions prevent convergence into closed optimization?
Perfect prediction is not necessarily the target; inability to be surprised is framed as loss of meaningful updating.
Feedback access, representation quality, adaptation depth, boundary classification, historical-transition causality and closure thresholds remain unresolved.
Long-term evolvability is proposed to require causal, epistemic and ontological permeability; nested dependence and later adaptive decline under closure are hypotheses.
Adaptive-boundary permeability plus P_C, P_E and O_C definitions.
Examples for high/low causal and epistemic permeability and language/mathematics/programming as ontological-permeability illustrations.
P_C -> P_E -> O_C hierarchy; capability-up/permeability-down closure pattern; permeability -> correction -> adaptation -> structural evolution -> evolvability.
Healthy optimization retains correction; closed optimization increases performance while correction disappears.
Permeability is explicitly a family of potentially measurable properties, not yet a single scalar; measurement formalization is future work.
Candidate empirical indicators for P_C, P_E and O_C.
Measurement formalization, causal hierarchy, units/thresholds, historical examples, indicator validity and openness/stability tradeoffs remain unresolved.

Representational limits are proposed as deep adaptive constraints; richer representation may enlarge search spaces; boundary shifts may precede major transitions; representation expansion is linked to ontological permeability.
Representation boundary, D_R, D_R* and C_R definitions.
reality -> representation -> decision space -> action -> feedback; candidate D_R*=D_R*C_R; capability-up/D_R*-down representation-collapse pattern.
Distinction precedes optimization; information accumulation is distinct from adaptive representation expansion.
Representation defines optimization space; evolution is framed as changing searchable spaces rather than merely searching them.
Encyclopedia, mathematics, programming, language and computation are used to contrast information accumulation with representation-space expansion.
D_R/D_R*/C_R estimators, dimensional validity, historical causal attribution, phase-transition criteria and O_C causal relation remain unresolved.
